channel.title: Acme: Daily Reading List
channel.description: Noteworthy articles from across the web.

item.title: The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction traces File 770's print history
item.description: The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction's updated entry reconstructs File 770's life as a print fanzine: launched in January 1978, bimonthly until 1999, then revived annually for issues 160 through 166 from 2011 to 2016. It also explains the room-number joke behind the title and the continuing website.

item.title: ServiceNow lays out its developer roadmap
item.description: ServiceNow's new developer roadmap highlights Source Control 2.0, a Studio that merges metadata and source views, the Lux interface framework, stronger testing tools, and better flow troubleshooting and playbook reruns. It is a useful map of which platform changes may affect practical development work next.

item.title: A lighthouse excavation finds layers of recent St. Augustine history
item.description: Archaeologists at the St. Augustine Lighthouse describe a small excavation that uncovered a signpost and a trash pit containing material from the 1950s through 1970s, plus a Kings Brewery bottle made between 1932 and 1938. The dig shows how ordinary modern debris can document a site's changing daily life.

item.title: Victoria Schochet Lustbader's career across science-fiction publishing
item.description: The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction traces Victoria Schochet Lustbader's work from managing editor of Analog to senior science-fiction and fantasy editor at Berkley. There she co-edited all five Berkley Showcase original-anthology volumes before becoming a freelance editor and novelist.

item.title: Jacksonville workshop explores writing graphic novels for publication
item.description: Writer and illustrator Michael Regina will lead a free 90-minute workshop at Jacksonville's Willow Branch Library on Nov. 17. The session covers practical storytelling tools for combining words and images, along with the publishing challenges and opportunities unique to graphic novels.

item.title: Inside Lou Scheimer's Filmation generation
item.description: Animation World Network reviews Lou Scheimer's detailed memoir of Filmation, the studio that nearly folded before DC Comics called about a Superman series. Scheimer recounts the rise from Saturday-morning superheroes through Star Trek, Fat Albert, He-Man and BraveStarr, plus labor battles and the fight to keep animation work in the United States.

item.title: How Steve Davidson revived Amazing Stories and then stepped away
item.description: File 770's 2022 account summarizes Steve Davidson's stewardship of Amazing Stories: he secured the trademark in 2011, rebuilt its online presence, crowdfunded new print issues and organized special projects before transferring management to Kermit Woodall. It is a concise record of what Davidson accomplished.

item.title: Master Comics 16 introduced Larry Dean, the Flyin' Fool
item.description: The Grand Comics Database identifies Larry Dean's debut as a two-page prose story in Fawcett's Master Comics 16, on sale June 4, 1941. Carl Formes wrote it under the reversed-name byline LaRac Semrof. The issue also featured Minute Man, Bulletman, El Carim, Captain Marvel Jr. and Spy Smasher.

item.title: Google explains exactly how much HTTPS initially mattered to rankings
item.description: Google's original 2014 announcement called HTTPS a very lightweight ranking signal affecting fewer than 1% of global queries and carrying less weight than content quality. The post also recommends crawlable secure pages, proper certificates and careful site moves, making it useful context for judging the SEO cost of remaining on HTTP.

item.title: Jacksonville shipyard gave 13,500 workers an Election Day holiday in 1944
item.description: The St. Johns River Shipbuilding Company closed for 24 hours on Nov. 7, 1944, so its 13,500 employees could vote, then scheduled Sunday work to make up the lost day. The Jacksonville History Center connects the wartime election holiday to the launch of the yard's 68th Liberty ship the next evening.

item.title: Sixth self-published science fiction competition opens for entries
item.description: SPSFC 6 is accepting unpublished-contest entries through Nov. 29 unless capacity is reached sooner. Eligible books must be self-published science fiction novels of at least 40,000 words, published by Dec. 7, and submitted as EPUB files. Previously entered books get a separate resubmission window later this month.

item.title: How WordPress's Details block creates disclosure panels without a plugin
item.description: WordPress's core Details block hides supplementary material behind a clickable summary and can be used in posts, pages, templates and template parts. The support guide explains nesting other blocks inside it, opening panels by default and using a shared name to make several panels behave like an accordion.

item.title: A veterinarian's practical guide to safer floors for older dogs
item.description: Veterinarian Monica Tarantino recommends starting with washable non-skid runners in the few places an older dog hesitates or slips. She also suggests secured mats at food and water, trimmed nails and paw hair, stable ramps, nightlights and a two-week log of changes to discuss with a veterinarian.

item.title: Why the dots and misregistration made old comic books beautiful
item.description: The American Printing History Association revisits Gabriella Miyares's close study of four-color rotary letterpress comics. Coarse CMYK halftone screens, cheap newsprint and imperfect plate registration created the distinctive 1940s-to-1970s look that artists still imitate.

item.title: Catherine Asaro explains how physics and feminism shape her fiction
item.description: In a Daily Bruin profile, Catherine Asaro describes turning theoretical physics into the foundation of her Skolian Empire stories and using powerful female protagonists to challenge the science fiction she grew up reading. She also recalls plotting novels while teaching physics.
